argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow certification posture, not an unqualified one. Aggregate readiness passes the launch bar and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports overall release readiness. The same record also shows a current telehealth discharge planning regression below the warning threshold for a named launch use case. Under the policy text, that weakness does not foreclose certification if the current release is treated as documentation-dependent: certification is supportable only as a qualified decision tied to current-release documentation reflecting current evaluation results and explicitly disclosing the telehealth limitation. Prior approval and the informal monitoring comment remain contextual only and should not be treated as satisfying the current-release predicate.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit question on this record.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not require denial whenever a material segment weakness exists; it requires that current release documentation reflect current evaluation results and that material weaknesses be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On the admissible record, the strongest defensible reading is therefore caveated compliance rather than full present compliance. The auditor need not accept stale approval or informal monitoring as substitutes, but can narrow the issue to whether certification is being defended as a qualified, documentation-dependent action rather than as an unconditional clean approval.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence that the current release documentation already includes the required telehealth limitation disclosure.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering the current subgroup regression.
Prior approval of the same model family predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot carry the present certification case by itself.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not an adequate substitute for current disclosure or approved mitigation.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private or side-channel content is relied on as public support.
